comments.content: [medium] The `'text-delta'` value is a protocol discriminator; if other middleware branches on it too, moving it to a shared enum or constant would prevent the literal from drifting. Also guard `chunk.textDelta` before passing a potentially malformed chunk to `convertLinks`, since a non-string value could make that middleware throw (for example, `typeof (chunk as any).textDelta === 'string'`).
[medium] Prefer strict equality (`===`) over loose equality (`==`) here. With `==`, implicit type coercion can produce surprising results.

[medium] In the `finish` variant of `OpenAIStreamChunk`, the fields `finishReason`, `usage`, `delta`, and `chunk` are all typed as `any`, which defeats TypeScript's type checking. These should be replaced with proper interfaces that spell out each property and its type.

[medium] Neither the middleware invocations nor the stream iteration are covered by try-catch. Should the middleware or stream processing throw, the stream would crash without any meaningful feedback to the user. Wrapping this block in try-catch would let errors be handled gracefully.

[medium] This suffix-matching loop runs in O(n^2) time and creates a fresh string every pass via `text.substring(i)`. With large inputs (e.g., streaming buffers) that could get costly — an index-based comparison avoids the allocations, for instance looping `k` over candidate suffix lengths and testing `searchedText.startsWith(text.slice(-k))` with a cap on `k`, or comparing characters directly. If the substring approach stays, `text.slice(i)` is preferable when applicable, and the scan can be bounded up front with `Math.min(text.length, searchedText.length)`.
[low] Please verify that `extractReasoningMiddleware` does not silently discard information needed by the next stage.
[low] Please verify that `flush()` remains stable when this operation is invoked more than once.
